items.title: Foundry's furnace bucket made a Vehicle (worked example)
items.what_thugpro_did: Reclassed THPS3's Obj_Bucket as Class=Vehicle with its own model Obj_Bucket.mdl, whose node array holds the collision geometry TRG_g_Bucket and a kill trigger TRGP_KillSkaterBucket; it moves by Obj_MoveToNode / Obj_RotX (CJR_Foun_Bucket_MoveOut). Its Obj_Bucket_Brace is a LevelObject with '//GameObject' commented out, so a GameObject was tried and dropped.
items.why_its_a_hack: Vehicle pulls in the whole car set from car_add_components (rail manager, skitch, object hook manager), so the bucket can be skitched, and it crashed when the model's .qb node array was missing (docs/pending/foun-crash.md). The kill trigger calls FOUN_BucketKillSkater01, which uses THUGPRO's TP_DoFlash; we leave that script out, so in our port touching the molten bucket does nothing.
items.better_approach: Keep THPS3's object as the LevelObject our converter already makes (its sector drawn) and give it CollisionMode=Geometry. The collision component's LevelObject branch (0x0041C7B0) then takes the level collision object of the same name, which TPN-THPS3-1 already adds as 'Obj_Bucket' (134 faces). Note for the agent doing this now: THUG2's own levels never put CollisionMode on a GameObject (it only works through gameobj_add_components), so LevelObject is the THUG2 way; Vehicle is THUG2's way only for movers that carry rails or trigger nodes (Barcelona's drawbridges). Write our own FOUN_BucketKillSkater01 using SK3_KillSkater nodename=TRG_Restart_6P plus a THUG2 flash or pulse_blur, run by the trigger faces.

items.title: Tokyo's bullet trains and planes forced to exist online, on random timers
items.what_thugpro_did: Made the shinkansen and planes Vehicles, removed AbsentInNetGames from 185 path waypoints, and creates the trains with THUGPRO_ForceCreate (a DLL command that ignores AbsentInNetGames) after 'Wait Random(4/6/8/10) seconds' (tok_Scripts.q JS_BulletTrainEastControl_Spawned). The trains follow paths with Obj_FollowPathLinked at 700-800 mph.
items.why_its_a_hack: AbsentInNetGames is kept on the node and overridden by a special create command, so the flag no longer means what it says. The random wait runs on each client separately, so every player sees the trains at different times. A THUGPRO player can be hit by a train the other players never see.
items.better_approach: If trains are wanted online, clear AbsentInNetGames on the train nodes and start them deterministically: the host decides the timing, or both clients use a fixed schedule keyed to the game's start. Our engine also has to support path following in network games (the 0x004695D0 crash in level-port-compromises section 3: no path manager there), which the decomp can now fix. Otherwise keep the trains offline-only on both sides.
items.evidence: THUGPRO source levels/tok/tok_Scripts.q:89-120; our replace_calls THUGPRO_ForceCreate -> Create (docs/pending/thps3-thugpro.md); level-port-compromises.md section 3 'An object following a path in a network game'.
items.online_impact: parity: moving hazards that knock players off. THUGPRO runs them online; ours, with ForceCreate mapped to Create, does not. Even THUGPRO clients disagree with each other on when a train passes.
items.status_in_our_port: same as THUGPRO: offline only (checked 2026-10-21, see correction)
items.correction: Wrong premise (docs/pending/thps3-bucket-cars-trains.md): THUGPRO_ForceCreate is not a DLL command but THUGPRO's global script (thugpro_utils.q: Create, or Kill + Create when the object is alive) - a plain Create, which THUG2 gates on AbsentInNetGames in a network or multi-player game (0x005A4DA0 -> 0x00565BB0). THUGPRO's trains and planes keep AbsentInNetGames (its tok.q), so THUGPRO does not create them online either: both sides agree (offline only) and no engine change is needed. Its random 4-10 s waits run offline, in each player's own game.

items.title: Invisible 'carplant_collision' vehicles locked on top of each car
items.what_thugpro_did: For each of Rio's 8 cars (and Suburbia's ice-cream truck) it adds a second, invisible Vehicle (CarPlantNode / CarPlantNode_Bus model: a trigger LevelGeometry TRGP_CarPlant01). It is glued to the car with Obj_LockToObject at an offset like (0,60,50) and polls ObjectExists every 4 frames. The car's own script kills it and re-creates it with THUGPRO_ForceCreate.
items.why_its_a_hack: THUGPRO's Rio cars use THPS3 car models that have no collision or car-plant triggers, so a separate shadow object stands in for them. In our port the cars are THUG2's own vehicles (PC-THPS3-10), whose model node arrays already carry collision, rails and Gap_CarHop triggers (veh_sedan.qb: Car, Car_WheelNN, TRGP_Sedan01-04). So the shadow objects add a second collision and trigger on every car.
items.better_approach: Leave the carplant_collision nodes, models and scripts out of our port while our cars are THUG2's (an op-remove port change, or a _left_out rule in thugpro_new_extract). If we later use THPS3's original car models (the exact-assets policy), give each car model its own node array with collision and TRGP car-hop trigger nodes, as THUG2's veh_*.qb do, rather than a locked second object.
items.evidence: THUGPRO source levels/rio/rio.q:22515-22554 and :26215 (ForceCreate before Car_Generic01); our rio.qb in C:\Games\THUG2-2 (TRG_Car_*_carplant_collisionScript = Obj_LockToObject + poll loop); THUG2 models\veh\veh_sedan\veh_sedan.qb.
items.online_impact: none (client-side): the cars and their shadows are AbsentInNetGames on both sides
items.correction: The shadow's collision is trigger-only (CarPlantNode.col.xbx: 12 faces, flags 0x50 = trigger + non-collidable) - no second solid collision. Its trigger runs THUGPRO_TriggerCarPlant (a THUGPRO global script: LaunchEvent Carplant on the skater), which ours hasn't, so in ours it was an inert invisible box (docs/pending/thps3-bucket-cars-trains.md).

items.title: Invisible 'collfix' / '_coll' collision laid over ramps and walls
items.what_thugpro_did: Added invisible collision objects on top of THPS3 geometry: Suburbia's SUB_TRamp04/06_collfix, SUB_plywood_08_collfix, SUB_HHBYardWall_collfix (192 faces) and Inviso_PicnicCollide01_collfix, replacing THPS3's Inviso_PicnicCollide01, which it switched off. Foundry gets SouthDeck_QP01/QP04_coll and Trench_HP04_Back_coll (4 faces each).
items.why_its_a_hack: Extra invisible faces patch surfaces that skated wrong in THUGPRO's conversion of THPS3's .bsp, instead of fixing that collision. If our converter already produces those surfaces correctly, the overlays leave doubled, almost coplanar faces that can snag or bump the skater.
items.better_approach: Compare each overlay with our converted collision at the same place (col_check plus a face-by-face diff) and find what THUGPRO was fixing: missing back faces, winding, quarter-pipe lips. Where ours is right, drop the overlay or merge it into the original object. Where ours is broken too, fix the converter, which helps every THPS3 level and not just these spots.

Online, a turning wheel would need synchronised rotation, so a frozen wheel with static rails is the pragmatic parity choice. Check that our port actually draws the cars: the THAW record says we make no ferris cars, which would leave TP-8's rails hanging in the air.

items.title: Doors and the garage elevator rebuilt as LevelObjects at run time (elevator shifted -25 by script)
items.what_thugpro_did: At level start its dynamic-level-changes script Kills London's 4 garage elevator doors and TRG_ParkingGarrage_Elevator and re-creates them with CreateFromStructure as LevelObject CollisionMode=Geometry, the elevator offset by (0,0,-25). The doors then slide with Obj_MoveToRelPos. College's elevator doors were simply moved 48 units to stand open (TP-22).
items.why_its_a_hack: Static node data is patched at run time (kill and re-create, a positional offset applied by script) instead of being written into the level. Every load repeats it, and it races with anything else that runs at level start.
items.better_approach: Bake it in at conversion: give those nodes Class=LevelObject, CollisionMode=Geometry and CreatedAtStart in the node array, and apply the -25 to the elevator's Pos / sector. This is how THUG2 (BO_Subway03) and our THPS4 ports' own moving pieces (jnk TRG_Crane01_*) are written. Keep only the door open / close scripts.

items.title: Host level options' default state set by running '<LVL>_LEVEL_CHANGE_0n off' at every start
items.what_thugpro_did: Its HandleLevelOptionObjects runs each option's toggle with off at every game start, which Kills or Creates geometry and rails: Shipyard's barge killed, San Francisco's rooftop objects killed, Zoo's hippo bridge up, London's race track killed in net games, Minneapolis' garage on. The THUG1 _thugpro.qb files are copied but never run.
items.why_its_a_hack: The level's resting state lives in a script rather than in CreatedAtStart. Geometry is created and then killed on every load, and the THUG1 option files are dead data in our build.

Leave out the THUG1 _thugpro.qb copies until something runs them. The current approach is defensible because it keeps one code path for both states.

items.title: Occluders and visibility-set triggers switched off
items.what_thugpro_did: Turned off LV's 15 occluders (CreatedAtStart) and RU's 4 occluders (the Occluder flag and CreatedAtStart), and emptied 69 of NJ's 85 occlusion / vis / proximity trigger scripts that Kill / Create occluders and visibility sets.

items.title: Elevators faked by teleports (random message, sound, jump boost)

A real moving elevator (a LevelObject with Obj_MoveToNode, like BO_Subway03) would look better but would make players' positions on the platform depend on each client's timing. Keep the teleports.

items.title: Radius triggers created at run time as ghost GameObjects
items.what_thugpro_did: Its level-start script does CreateFromStructure for a model-less GameObject per trigger, tags it with a radius and a script, and installs an AnyObjectInRadius handler. Some are skipped in KOTH / CTF.
items.why_its_a_hack: Nodes that could be static are injected at run time from a data list (_LevelChanges), so they are invisible to the node array, the level editor and our tools.
items.better_approach: Emit them as nodes at conversion: a GameObject Type=Ghost model="none" CreatedAtStart whose TriggerScript sets the inner / outer radius and the handler. This is the pattern our THPS3 converter already uses for proximity watchers. The KOTH / CTF skip stays in the script. The run-time form works; this only tidies it.

items.title: THUGPRO_SafeKill / THUGPRO_ForceCreate wrappers
items.what_thugpro_did: SafeKill kills only when the object exists. ForceCreate creates even when AbsentInNetGames says not to (in its DLL).
items.why_its_a_hack: SafeKill guards THUG2's crash on killing a missing or collision-only object. ForceCreate overrides the network flag instead of setting the flag right.
items.better_approach: SafeKill as an IsAlive guard is how THUG2's own scripts do it (if IsAlive / ObjectExists), so ours is fine. Longer term the decomp can make Kill / Visible tolerate missing or sector-less objects (level-port-compromises section 3: CFunc_Visible 0x5A5050). Our ForceCreate -> Create mapping changes the meaning online: record that in the register (see tok-trains-forcecreate-online).
items.evidence: tools/thps4_levels/thugpro_new.ts thps4_tp_safe_kill / thps4_tp_force_create; docs/pending/thps3-thugpro.md:269-272.
items.online_impact: parity only where ForceCreate brings an object online on THUGPRO's side (Tokyo's trains; Rio's carplants, which are absent anyway)

items.title: Kona's 19 level lights at Brightness 0, lit only by THUGPRO's night system
items.what_thugpro_did: Added TRG_Night_LevelLight_thugpro_* with Brightness 0, which THUGPRO's time-of-day script raises at night.
items.why_its_a_hack: The lights only make sense with THUGPRO's TOD driver. In ours they are 19 dead nodes.
items.better_approach: Harmless while there is no TOD system. If we ever port THPS4 lighting or a TOD of our own, drive these with THUG2's TODManager like THUG2's own LevelLight nodes. Otherwise they could be left out.
items.evidence: tools/compat/thugpro/README.md TP-27; THUG2 BA / BE / BO LevelLight nodes (205 / 222 / 195) with TODManager_ResetLevelLights.
items.online_impact: none (client-side)

items.title: Toolchain renames: zone prefix stripped from 226 nodes, clusters re-prefixed, 'bastardrail1'
items.what_thugpro_did: Stripped the zone prefix from EL / SM night lights, added the zone prefix to DN / JA / SZ clusters, renamed CH's goal letters, and renamed SZ's PBoatPostEvent_TRG_2214 to bastardrail1.
items.why_its_a_hack: These are toolchain artefacts and an ad-hoc name, not design.
items.better_approach: Node names don't travel, so the node renames could be dropped. Cluster names may travel: graffiti and trick-object messages name the cluster. Keeping THUGPRO's cluster names is right for parity, and the register already treats them so.
items.evidence: tools/compat/thugpro/README.md TP-5 / TP-6 ('graffiti names a cluster').
items.online_impact: parity for clusters (graffiti / trick attack); none for node names

items.title: NetEnabled / Permanent taken off breakables and objects
items.what_thugpro_did: Took NetEnabled off Warehouse's secret-room glass and SI's sponsors, and NetEnabled / Permanent off Shipyard's 6 sound and breakaway pieces.
items.why_its_a_hack: Taking the network-sync flag off makes breaking local, so one player can see glass the other has broken.
items.better_approach: THUG2's net sync of killed objects is what NetEnabled is for, but these pieces don't collide once broken (trigger or non-collidable faces), so local-only state is harmless. Both sides must agree on the flag either way.
items.evidence: tools/compat/thugpro/README.md TP-14 / TP-24.
items.online_impact: parity: whether a break is sent over the network. Both sides must use the same flags.

items.title: Venice's 58 sand kill zones call THUGPRO's own Sk3_Killskater_sand
items.what_thugpro_did: Replaced THUG1's Sk3_Killskater_Water with its own Sk3_Killskater_sand from thugpro_utils.qb (smashcake sound, extra death messages, sand colour).
items.why_its_a_hack: This is a cosmetic global-script addition, not a fix.
items.better_approach: It is a parameterised wrapper over THUG2's SK3_KillSkater_Finish, the same shape as THUG2's own SK3_KillSkater_Water. Fine as level content.
items.evidence: docs/pending/thug1.md:269-271.
items.online_impact: none (client-side): kills are local

items.title: Skate shop door kept closed by THPS4's invisible walls
items.what_thugpro_did: Kept THPS4's own invisible door walls (InvisColl01's shop side, Object10's two faces); its Open Fence host option force-creates them.
items.why_its_a_hack: It isn't one: this is THPS4's own data.
items.better_approach: THUGPRO's choice is the original's. Our open door is our own deviation for the main-menu backdrop (PC-THPS4-1/2). If parity in the shop matters, switch the walls on only for net games: create InvisColl01 when InNetGame.
items.evidence: tools/compat/thugpro/README.md TP-29.
items.online_impact: parity: our players ride through a doorway that is a wall for THUGPRO's
items.status_in_our_port: we already differ (PC-THPS4-1 / PC-THPS4-2; TP-29 off)

items.title: Natas-spin points as single unlinked rail nodes
items.what_thugpro_did: Added single RailNodes with no links (TRG_TP_VN_Natas_1-3, SC2's 11, RU's natas_streetlamps, Zoo's TRG_NatasNode_01-05). SZ's parking meters got a natas check.
items.why_its_a_hack: It looks like fake rails, but it isn't a hack.
items.better_approach: THUG2's own levels use isolated rail nodes for spin points (BA 315, ST 66, NO 56: AU's TRG_TrashCanSpin01-03, BO's TRG_Rail_Tsign02-04), so this is the native mechanism.
items.evidence: THUG2 AU.qb / BO.qb / BA.qb unlinked RailNodes (counted with a node-array scan).
items.online_impact: parity: grindable / spinnable points. Both sides have them.

items.title: NJ's El train and Hawaii's boat as Vehicles
items.what_thugpro_did: Added the El train (its own model veh_El_Train, moving between TRG_TrainTest waypoints) and HI's boat (THUG2's own veh_ba_boat) as Class=Vehicle, AbsentInNetGames.
items.why_its_a_hack: Same pattern as the bucket, but these are vehicles.
items.better_approach: THUG2 itself makes its tram and boat Vehicles (BA TRG_BA_Bridge_Boat01 Class=Vehicle Type=Boat with veh_ba_boat.qb carrying collision and wood rails; ncomp_Vehicle_1420 Type=Tram). Check that veh_El_Train's .qb comes along (it does: 1.8 KB), or it would hit the foun crash.
items.evidence: THUG2 BA.qb TRG_BA_Bridge_Boat01; models\veh\ba\veh_ba_boat\veh_ba_boat.qb; docs/pending/thug1.md:255-260.
items.online_impact: none (client-side): AbsentInNetGames on both sides

items.title: Skater Island's ocean sound objects replaced by emitters
items.what_thugpro_did: Removed THPS3's TRG_OceanNoise / 01 sound objects and added two EmitterObject nodes (TRG_SFX_SOB_OceanWaves01/02) with rewritten proximity scripts.
items.why_its_a_hack: It looks like swapping out original data, but it isn't a hack.
items.better_approach: EmitterObject is THUG2's own ambient-sound node (BA 32, BE 38, BO 36 of them), so this is the idiomatic THUG2 form of THPS3's ocean noise.
items.evidence: THUG2 node-array class counts (EmitterObject); tools/compat/thugpro/README.md TP-16.
items.online_impact: none (client-side)

items.title: Duplicate collision faces removed; THPS3's MEATALSMOOTH typo fixed
items.what_thugpro_did: Removed duplicate back faces (THPS3 SI / Ros / Ware: 61 faces; College: 607 faces in 69 objects) and fixed THPS3's TERRAIN_MEATALSMOOTH typo plus untyped rails.
items.why_its_a_hack: It isn't one: these are data cleanups.
items.better_approach: These are correct fixes. Doubled faces can snag the skater, and an unknown terrain reads through a null in THUG2 (the Tokyo crash). Our fixTerrains already did the typo fix.
items.evidence: tools/compat/thugpro/README.md TP-15 / TP-19 / TP-28.
items.online_impact: parity: the same surfaces on both sides

items.title: NY's 11 rails given TERRAIN_GRINDRUSTYRAIL, a terrain THUG2 hasn't
items.what_thugpro_did: Set 11 rails to TERRAIN_GRINDRUSTYRAIL.
items.why_its_a_hack: It's a bug rather than a hack: an unknown rail terrain makes THUG2 read through a null (the THPS3 Tokyo crash) unless THUGPRO's DLL adds the terrain.
items.better_approach: Keep THUG1's TERRAIN_GRINDMETAL, as we do (nodes.fixTerrains).
items.evidence: tools/compat/thugpro/README.md TP-35 'Not taken'; docs/pending/thug1.md:282.
items.online_impact: none (grind sound only)
